message.content:
**Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta.** Noise violations are handled by the City of Atlanta’s **Police Department** and the **City Code Enforcement** office. Here’s how you can do it: | Step | What to Do | Where to Go / Who to Call | |------|------------|---------------------------| | 1 | **Determine the type of noise** (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs, etc.). | — | | 2 | **File a complaint online** (most convenient). | Visit the City of Atlanta’s official website: → “Services” → “Noise Complaint.” You’ll find an online form that asks for details such as address, time, description, and your contact info. | | 3 | **Call the Atlanta Police Department** if you need immediate assistance or if the noise is ongoing. | • Non‑emergency line: **(404) 656‑4000** (for general inquiries)
• 911 for emergencies (e.g., violent disturbances). | | 4 | **Contact the City Code Enforcement Office** for repeated or severe violations. | • Phone: **(404) 656‑4000** (same line as above)
• Email: **code.enforcement@atlantaga.gov** | | 5 | **Follow up** if you haven’t heard back within a few days. | Use the same phone line or email; keep a record of your complaint reference number. | ### Quick Tips - **Provide specifics**: Address, exact time, description of the noise, and any evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings). - **Use the online form**: It automatically generates a reference number so you can track the status. - **If the noise is from a neighbor or a business**, you can also ask the property owner to comply with city noise ordinances before filing a formal complaint. ### Legal Background Atlanta’s noise ordinance is part of the **City of Atlanta Code, Title 10 – Public Safety, Chapter 10.1 – Noise**. Violations can result in fines or other penalties. The city council oversees the ordinance but the day‑to‑day enforcement is handled by the police and code enforcement teams. --- **Bottom line:** Yes, you can report a noise complaint to the City of Atlanta. Use the online form or call the non‑emergency police line, and you’ll be directed to the appropriate department for action.
